user_query: How does LINE-SGD differ from LINE in the way each model uses edge weights during optimization?
llm_response: LINE-SGD and LINE both learn node embeddings from graph edges, but they use edge weights differently during optimization. In LINE, an edge’s weight is treated as a frequency/probability signal: heavier edges are sampled more often, so they influence training indirectly through the sampling distribution. In LINE-SGD, the edge weight is used directly in the gradient update as a multiplicative importance factor, so each sampled edge contributes proportionally to its weight during optimization rather than only being reflected in how often it is sampled.
llm_confidence_reasoning: This matches the standard distinction between weighted edge sampling in LINE and weight-scaled stochastic gradient updates in LINE-SGD, though exact implementation details can vary by description.
